text:
Maria.AE: Posting here — BlueHarbor POC (internal: coraline trial). Customer wants to run coraline-30b on their on‑prem infra with KV prefix caching + HSM KMS. Need variant compatibility, rough ops timeline, and ballpark pricing for ~10 qps sustained. Any immediate blockers?

Tony.SE: Quick check — can we run coraline-30b with our q8_0 runtime? I remember coraline uses RMSNorm and grouped_gemm; last conversion had some fused ops. @Olivia.ML any notes?

Olivia.ML: short answer: coraline-30b (orig) uses grouped_gemm + RMSNorm. We have a q8_0 fallback but the precompiled kernels in runtime v2 don't hit the grouped_gemm perf path — quantized v2 will run but needs conversion script + recompile. KV prefix caching supported up to ~2048 tokens; beyond that we need kv-shard changes.

Kyle.Infra: For Private/on‑prem customers they must have NVIDIA driver >= 525 and CUDA 12.1+. Also need host libraries for PKCS#11 if using HSM. If they pick Dedicated we handle infra. @Maria.AE do they have exact specs?

Maria.AE: Customer says they can provision 2x A100S or 4x H100s depending on budget and want the instance inside a locked datacenter. They expect enterprise SLA + 24/7 support. Can we do 99.9% for Private + on‑call?

Tony.SE: We can offer a support add‑on for 24/7. SLA for Dedicated is standard (99.95). For Private we typically do platform fee + support contract; SLA is negotiated. Rough ballpark for 4x H100s hosted: ~$450/hr platform (ballpark) + ops. I'll calculate a precise 10 qps estimate.

Olivia.ML: Onboarding estimate (hands‑on): model conversion + quantization + compile + basic perf bake: 3 business days. KV stress/perf tuning: 1 day. Docs + integration checks: 1 day. Total ~5 business days. Canary/A-B rollouts add ~2 days.

infra-bot: INF ticket created: INF-8421 for driver/CUDA validation. Run on customer host: \n```\nkubectl apply -f driver-version-check.yaml
./validate_cuda.sh --min 12.1
```\n
Tony.SE: Security RFI — they require HSM with PKCS#11 key wrap and no-key-leak guarantees. @Ollie.Security can we support that in Private? Also which compliance artifacts should we send (SOC2, dataflow, pen test)?

Ollie.Security: OlliE.Security: We support customer‑provided HSM via PKCS#11 in Private using our KMS shim. Required deliverables: completed security questionnaire, network diagram, and signed DPA. We can provide SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary. Note: if they require zero‑egress model residency, we need to validate storage behaviour. I'll post the Private onboarding checklist link: https://redwood.internal/onboard/private-checklist (internal).

Maria.AE: Next steps — I'll ask them for infra spec, CUDA/driver output, and the filled RFI. Tony — please prepare a 10 qps cost calc + SOW draft. Olivia — tentatively block 2 full days for conversion once we greenlight. Ollie — I'll DM the RFI when returned. :thumbsup:

Tony.SE: Will do. Ping me if they lean Dedicated vs Private — cost delta is material.

Olivia.ML: If they are flexible on fidelity we can offer a distilled variant (coraline-lite, ~13B) which reduces memory and cost significantly with modest quality tradeoffs. Good option if budget constrained.

Maria.AE: Thanks team — I'll update after I have driver output and the RFI.
